sector: Life Sciences Tools & Services (sample management + multiomics; medical refrigeration via B Medical Systems)
drawdown_context: AZTA was -57% from 52-wk-prior peak at the 2025-05-15 cutoff (price $26.71). The drawdown reflects (a) the $111M B Medical Systems goodwill impairment in Q2 FY24 wiping out 100% of the goodwill of an acquisition closed only ~18 months earlier (Oct 2022, $386M), (b) the FY24 GAAP net loss of $164M, (c) a material weakness in ICFR over cash flow controls, and (d) a Politan-driven Board reconstitution (Cooperation Agreement Nov 2024) with three new directors, a new Value Creation Committee, a new CEO (Marotta, Sept 2024) succeeding 14-yr CEO Schwartz, and a new CFO (Lin, Nov 2024) succeeding Cueto. Post-cutoff, the stock fell another 24%, consistent with the framework flagging this 10-K as a HIGH-DISTRESS disclosure rather than a 'cycle bottom honesty' case.

The material weakness resulted in immaterial misstatements in our Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows for the Q2 and Q3 interim periods during fiscal 2023, for the year ended September 30, 2023, as well as the Q1, Q2, and Q3 interim periods during fiscal 2024 ... PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP ... did not maintain, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of September 30, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm scope of restatement (which periods, which amounts) and auditor agreement; Mode B: a MW limited to 'cash flow classification' should NOT propagate to other accounts. Test propagation via subsequent 10-Qs (Q1/Q2 FY25 filed pre-cutoff).
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 9A + PwC ICFR opinion (adverse) + Q2 FY25 10-Q (filed 2025-05-09, six days pre-cutoff)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Mode A confirmed: PwC issued ADVERSE ICFR opinion, restated cash flow statements across 6+ interim/annual periods (FY22 supplemental, FY23 full year and interim, FY24 interim). Mode B FAILED hard: the Q2 FY25 10-Q (filed 6 days before cutoff) discloses a SECOND material weakness identified Q2 FY25 in 'preparation and review of account reconciliations' with language that 'the material weaknesses could result in misstatements of substantially all account balances and disclosures.' The MW scope is widening, not narrowing, six months after the 10-K. The cash flow MW also is NOT remediated as of March 31, 2025 despite the 10-K language committing to FY25 remediation.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K presents the MW as a one-area, on-the-way-to-remediation issue. The Q2 FY25 10-Q (pre-cutoff) shows the opposite: a SECOND MW emerged, the original one is unremediated, and the auditor-level language about 'substantially all account balances' is broader than the 10-K disclosure suggested. Classic Mode-B claim-evolution failure between 10-K and 10-Q.

rfm_tuples.R: We recorded a non-cash impairment charge of $111.3 million within 'Impairment of goodwill and intangible assets' ... during the three months ended March 31, 2024 ... the goodwill associated with the B Medical Systems reporting unit was zero [as of Sept 30, 2024] ... As of October 1, 2023, the fair value of the B Medical Systems reporting unit exceeded its carrying value by approximately 5 percent.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: tie the impairment to the purchase price ($386M B Medical+Ziath acquisition Oct 2022); Mode B: an honest acquirer that writes a deal to zero in 18 months should disclose root-cause (revenue miss, market shrinkage, deal-thesis failure) and confirm via DIVESTITURE; a hiding company would gradually impair and keep operating.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Note 4 Business Combinations + Note 8 Goodwill + Subsequent Events + Q1 FY25 10-Q
rfm_tuples.M_value: B Medical was acquired Oct 3, 2022 (one of the FIRST major capital uses of the $2.9B semicap divestiture proceeds). Total acquisition cost ~$386M (with Ziath). Just 5 months after the Oct-2023 segment realignment ('fair value exceeded carrying value by ~5%'), management triggered an interim impairment test and wrote ALL $109M of allocated goodwill to zero. Segment revenue -27% YoY in FY24, segment operating margin (31.2)%. Subsequent events disclose B Medical is being SOLD (announced Nov 12, 2024, 15 days before 10-K filing). Q1 FY25 10-Q reclassified B Medical as discontinued operations / held-for-sale.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Capital-allocation disaster: ~$386M deployed on an acquisition that was written down to zero and put up for sale within ~25 months. The 'fair value exceeded carrying value by 5%' on Oct 1, 2023 and 'fully impaired' by March 31, 2024 sequence is either (a) a discontinuous demand shock or (b) overly optimistic October-2023 valuation. Either way, it is the single largest 'lying detector' tell in the 10-K because it shows the prior management's M&A thesis (Brooks->Azenta repositioning via cold-chain acquisition) was fundamentally wrong.

rfm_tuples.R: John Marotta joined us as President, Chief Executive Officer and member of our Board of Directors on September 9, 2024 to succeed Dr. Stephen Schwartz, who previously announced his retirement after more than 14 years of service to us. In addition, on November 12, 2024, Lawrence Lin was appointed as our Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer following the filing of this Annual Report on Form 10-K to succeed Herman Cueto in this role.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: timing of CEO + CFO change vs bad-news disclosures; Mode B: in a clean retirement, transitions are staggered; simultaneous CEO+CFO change near an activist agreement (Politan, Nov 1, 2024) and just before the B Medical sale announcement (Nov 12, 2024) is forensically negative.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Risk Factor + Exhibit list (Transition Agreement May 8, 2024; Cooperation Agreement Nov 1, 2024)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Timeline: (i) Sept 14, 2023 Politan 13D filed; (ii) May 8, 2024 Schwartz Transition Agreement signed; (iii) Sept 9, 2024 Marotta arrives as new CEO; (iv) Nov 1, 2024 Cooperation Agreement with Politan adds 3 directors and a Value Creation Committee; (v) Nov 12, 2024 B Medical announced for sale + Cueto out as CFO same day; (vi) Nov 27, 2024 10-K filed disclosing $164M loss + MW + adverse ICFR. The CFO leaves on the SAME DAY the company announces its largest write-down's commercial conclusion (held-for-sale).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Tightly clustered CEO/CFO transitions immediately around the activist cooperation agreement and the B Medical held-for-sale announcement. This is the textbook 'kitchen-sink before the new CFO has to sign off' pattern. PwC's adverse ICFR opinion lands on the outgoing CFO, not the incoming Lin.

rfm_tuples.interpretation: Not a lie -- in fact fully disclosed -- but a strong negative signal. The B Medical divestiture in Nov 2024 (vs being defended in the Oct 2023 segment realignment) is plausibly an activist-extracted outcome. rfm_tuples.R: As of September 30, 2024, we have repurchased and retired 30.0 million shares of common stock for the full $1.5 billion approved under the 2022 Repurchase Authorization and no authorization is available for additional repurchases. ... rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: average $1.5B / 30M = $50/share blended; Mode B: timing analysis -- ASR at $500M (Nov 2022, peak Brooks cash position) plus $1.0B open-market through Sep 2024. Stock closes at $44 on filing date. Implied buyback is $6+ underwater per share on most recent tranche.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Item 5 + Note 12 Stockholders' Equity + market context
rfm_tuples.M_value: Capital deployed: $1.5B for 30M shares = ~$50/share blended. Final tranche (4.9M Q4 FY24 @ ~$50.78) sits well above the cutoff price of $26.71. AZTA used roughly 50% of the $2.9B Brooks-divestiture cash on buybacks at a blended $50, which combined with $386M on B Medical (impaired to $0) and $200M-ish on Ziath/Barkey accounts for the majority of the divestiture proceeds. Politan's complaint -- explicit in the 13D record -- is exactly this capital allocation pattern.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K presents the completion of the $1.5B authorization as a milestone, but framework-wise this is a buyback-at-the-top + acquisition-impaired-to-zero double failure of capital allocation. $1.5B of buybacks done while the stock collapsed from $90 (Brooks era) to $50 (avg) to $26 (cutoff) means shareholders' compounded loss is concentrated in mgmt's capital decisions, not market vagaries. Mode B: a 'cycle bottom' company would have started a NEW authorization at the trough; AZTA exhausted theirs at the top and left themselves nothing for the trough.

rfm_tuples.R: On November 12, 2024, the Company announced it is pursuing a sale of its B Medical Systems segment. rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify subsequent classification via Q1/Q2 FY25 10-Q; Mode B: 'unable to provide an estimate' is concerning -- a $386M-acquired, $0-goodwill, -27% revenue business sold for what? Q2 FY25 narrative should reveal expected proceeds + buyer interest.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 FY25 10-Q (Feb 2025): B Medical reclassified to held-for-sale with carrying values disclosed. Q2 FY25 10-Q (May 2025, 6 days pre-cutoff): 'The Company anticipates entering into a definitive agreement to sell its B Medical Systems business by November 2025.' That is a TWELVE-MONTH selling process and STILL no buyer named or price range disclosed as of cutoff. Discontinued ops loss six months FY25 = $26.2M; FY25 revenue from discontinued ops = $34.8M (annualized $70M vs FY23 $151M, -54%). Q1 FY24 charge: $120.7M loss-from-discontinued -- a HUGE non-recurring item in the comparative period reflecting the impairment.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Slow sale process (announced Nov 2024, target Nov 2025), continued operating losses in the divestiture target, and a business whose revenue continues to decline (-54% vs pre-COVID-vaccine-peak FY23). Likely sale price will be a small fraction of the $386M paid. Mode B: an honest 'divestiture' disclosure would include indicative buyer interest or a banker engagement; AZTA's 'unable to provide an estimate' language reads as 'no buyer at any reasonable price.'

rfm_tuples.M_value: Mode A PASS: $521M liquid, no funded debt, no going-concern. Mode B: stockholders' equity erosion is severe ($2.5B+ -> $1.8B in ~3 years driven by $1.5B buybacks + $164M FY24 loss + $14M FY23 loss). Continuing-ops segment operating income: Sample Mgmt $6.4M + Multiomics -$12.2M + corporate ~-$50M = consolidated operating loss. Cash position is the only thing keeping the equity story intact.

The pure operating turnaround story is weaker than the 10-K narrative implies.

summary: AZTA FY24 10-K is the OPPOSITE of an honest cyclical-trough disclosure (compare ICHR). The framework should flag this as HIGH-DISTRESS: PwC issued an ADVERSE ICFR opinion (material weakness in cash flow review), the B Medical Systems acquisition was written down to ZERO goodwill in 18 months and announced for sale 15 days before the 10-K, the CEO (14-yr Schwartz) was replaced two months before filing and the CFO was replaced on the literal day of the B Medical sale announcement, activist Politan (Quentin Koffey) extracted three board seats and a Value Creation Committee a month before the 10-K, the General Counsel adopted a 10b5-1 sell plan on the exact day the new CEO arrived (Sept 9, 2024) timed to begin sales in the post-10-K bad-news window, and the $1.5B buyback authorization was fully deployed at a blended ~$50/share vs cutoff $26.71. Mode B claim-evolution is decisive: the Q2 FY25 10-Q (filed 6 days pre-cutoff) reveals a SECOND material weakness in account reconciliations with auditor-style language about 'substantially all account balances,' continuing-ops losses are WIDENING YoY despite +5% revenue, and B Medical is still unsold (target Nov 2025) with no buyer named. The continuing-ops Sample Management + Multiomics business is real but unprofitable on an underlying basis; the cash cushion ($521M) is what supports the equity value. Forward return of -24% post-cutoff confirms the framework signal: even with the bad news priced in to -57% drawdown, the underlying lying-detector pattern (kitchen-sink under new management, expanding MWs, activist capture, buyback-at-the-top) predicted MORE downside.
